name: 40. Bedrock Invoke Route Content-Block Cache Control (#5629)
description: Follow-up to the review comment on invoke.go:808 (part of #5629's fix): cache_control was handled for system messages (parseSystemMessages) and tools (convertAnthropicTools) but not for ordinary message content blocks, nor for cache_control nested inside a tool_result's own content array. applyMessageContentCacheControl/injectContentBlockCachePoints (invoke.go) now translate both cases into Bedrock Converse's positional cachePoint sibling entries, and convertSingleBedrockMessageToBifrostMessages (responses.go) was extended to propagate a nested tool_result CachePoint to the function_call_output message's CacheControl. Cases run write/read pairs against the same prefix per model — turn 1 creates a cache entry, turn 2 must read from it with cache_read_input_tokens/cached_tokens exceeding the fresh (uncached) token count, proving the cache read is HIGH, not just present. Covers plain content-block and nested-tool_result cache_control across three Anthropic-family models on Bedrock (Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.7), a multi-tool-call turn (two independent tool_result blocks, cache_control on only one), and a cross-provider sanity pass through Bedrock Mantle (Opus 4.8) via the unified /v1/chat/completions route — Bedrock Mantle traffic never goes through the buggy BedrockInvokeRequest.UnmarshalJSON code path (it's parsed by Anthropic's own request types, which were already correct), so these Mantle cases confirm the same capability works there too rather than pinning a regression. Cases also include the streaming variant (POST .../invoke-with-response-stream, Haiku 4.5 only) for both the plain content-block and nested-tool_result scenarios, decoding the AWS event-stream "bytes" framing to assert on message_delta.usage — request parsing (BedrockInvokeRequest.UnmarshalJSON) is identical between /invoke and /invoke-with-response-stream (Stream is set externally by the route handler, not from the JSON body), so this pins that the fix composes correctly with the streaming response path too, not just non-streaming.
